page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8y.2xlarge is an arm64 memory-optimized virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by Alibaba's custom YiTian710 processor operating at a fixed 2.75 GHz frequency. The configuration provides 8 dedicated physical cores with 8 vCPUs, utilizing single-threaded cores without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The server features no local disk storage, requiring network-attached block volumes, and includes no GPU acceleration. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier capabilities across general compute and memory pipelines. In synthetic CPU assessments, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1,820.48 and a multi-core score of 14,486.45, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 6,807.57. Memory throughput reaches 79.25 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 35.47 GB/sec for uncached writes. Application-level evaluations show 12.61 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 12.11 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Notable performance limitations appear in cryptography, where the PassMark encryption test placed in the bottom quartile at 1,327.33, as well as in 7B-parameter language model text generation, which achieved 8.3 tokens per second.

The hardware configuration offers high memory density per physical core, avoiding thread contention through dedicated vCPU allocation. This architecture is well structured for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, medium-scale relational database engines, and ETL processes requiring substantial memory capacity. It is less suited for workloads requiring hardware-assisted encryption acceleration, dedicated GPU processing, or high-speed local scratch storage.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network throughput of 5 Gbps.
